newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil steady on new crop arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil steady on new crop arrivals.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices were steady during the week with new summer crop arrivals and sufficient stocks of imported sunflower and palm olein oil, industry officials said on Wednesday.
"The market is unchanged due to good stocks and summer crop arrivals," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Industry officials said nearly 150,000 tonnes of sunflower oil from the United States and Argentina had already arrived. "But palm olein arrivals are slow," Shah said.
He said traders were not signing new import commitments as the summer crop had started arriving.
"Imports contracts will firm up again from June, July," Shah said.
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 34,200 rupees per tonne, soybean oil at 27,800, palm olein at 28,000 and sunflower oil (crude) at 25,000 rupees per tonne, largely unchanged from last week.
The annual Economic Survey for 1996/97 has forecast the 1996/97 (July-June) summer oilseeds crop at 9.7 million tonnes. Harvest of the summer crop began in February.
India harvests two oilseeds crops, getting the bulk of the output from the winter crop.
